thread:
sre-bot: [ALERT] realtime p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in us-east-1 · p99=1.83s (baseline ~320ms) · trigger: p99 > 1.5s for 5m · paging @maya :rotating_light:

maya: ack — seeing alerts, joining. pulling up dashboards now.

jordan: oncall here, pinged. any customer errors?

priya: error rate looks flat from metrics -> 0.2% (same as baseline). seems latency-only so far.

maya: confirmed — error budget unaffected but tail latency and streaming stalls up. inflight tokens per request spiked; KV cache hit-rate dropped ~40%.

sam: grabbing recent traces. quick check: last 10m traces show many > 1s on initial token generation step.

ken: could be kernel scheduling or one of the model variants hitting quantized path. checking runtime node pool.

infra-bot: autoscaler observed several backfill events in pool-gpu-us-east-1 around 06:02 UTC (nodes added: 4 -> 8).

maya: okay that aligns — scaling churn might be causing cold KV cache and increased latency for a subset. jordan can you confirm if we had a recent rollout to model-v3-quant?

jordan: yes we did a small canary at 05:55 UTC — rolled model-v3-quant to 10% of traffic in us-east-1. I can rollback immediately.

maya: before rollback, quick triage steps:
- check p95 vs p99 split on per-model and per-region
- confirm streaming stalls count and which route IDs affected
- check overload/backpressure signals from runtime logs

sam: dashboards: p95 only moved from 320ms -> 420ms; p99 moved to 1.83s. streaming tail stall count +240% on /v1/stream route. Affected mostly model-v3-quant variant.

priya: customer impact assessment: top-20 tenants (by qps) show latency uptick but no 5xxs. only degraded UX. no page to support yet.

maya: ok action plan proposal:
1) rollback model-v3-quant canary to 0% (jordan)
2) pause autoscaler for pool-gpu-us-east-1 to stabilize nodes (ken/infra)
3) enable KV-prefill for warm cache on active replicas (sam)
4) watch p99 for 10m and escalate if not improved

jordan: starting rollback now — will flip traffic off canary progressively.

ken: setting autoscaler to manual hold for 15m.

sam: issuing KV prefill job to active nodes (script snippet):
```
# run on controller
./tools/kv-prefill --region us-east-1 --model model-v3 --parallel 8 --limit 200
```

maya: thanks. also adding a short-lived route-level fallback to model-v2 for requests that hit streaming mode heavy and exceed 800ms. cordon: route /v1/stream fallback -> model-v2.

infra-bot: rollback complete at 06:08 UTC. canary traffic 0%.

jordan: confirmed rollback done, monitoring.

sam: KV prefill completed at 06:09 UTC. initial warm cache hit-rate recovered to 78% from 42%.

maya: monitoring p95/p99 now — p99 dropped to 420ms within 3m and trending down to ~350ms. p95 back to ~330ms.

priya: customer comms draft: "We observed a transient latency spike affecting streaming responses in us-east-1. Root cause: a canary rollout of a quantized model variant that interacted with autoscaling churn and KV cold-warm behavior. Mitigation: rollback and cache prefill. No customer requests failed; some experienced higher latency for ~10 minutes." anyone want to add?

ken: add note about autoscaler suspension and follow-up to adjust warmup hooks.

maya: putting this on the incident tracker INC-2026-1847 and creating a follow-up ticket to improve rollout gating and KV prefill automation.

jordan: should we add an automated detector rule to block model-variant canary if p99 jump > 2x baseline within 10m?

maya: yes — ticket that as action item. Also schedule a postmortem sync with runtime and infra next week.

priya: closing customer impact window at 06:20 UTC. no ongoing incidents.

maya: final checks — p99 stable at 340ms for last 5m. moving thread to archived watch. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-1847 created and linked to thread 5167894321.
